entries.title: Add everyone with a reviewer tag to a review plan in one step
entries.summary: The **Add reviewer** dialog on **Reviewers** has a new **By tag** tab: pick one or more reviewer tags (any or all), see who will be added and who is already on the plan, and add them all at once. Nobody is added twice.

where.path: Program → Review → Reviewers (or a plan's Reviewers tab) → Add → Add reviewer → By tag

entries.use_case: When a committee is already tagged by specialty, an admin can put the whole Cardiology panel on a new review plan in one click instead of adding people one at a time, and see exactly who will be added first.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: the By tag tab is in the Add reviewer dialog for every Review Plan 2.0 plan.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reuses the same tagged reviewer groups across plans, or complains about adding reviewers one by one.
internal.who_should_get_it: Sessions 2.0 customers with large review committees who tag reviewers (34 US events tag reviewers today).
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Reviewers → Add → Add reviewer → By tag
internal.gotchas: Tags must exist and be applied first (Reviewer tags tab). Only people on the Reviewers list match. With no round checked, people join the plan only — check rounds to enroll them. Invites follow the Send invite email switch, like a manual add.
internal.talk_track: If your reviewers are tagged, you can now add a whole tag to a plan at once — you'll see the list and how many are already on it before you confirm.

entries.title: Assign Awards reviewers to a round by tag
entries.summary: A round's **Reviewers** tab has **Assign by tag**: pick program reviewer tags (any or all), preview who joins the round and who is already on it, and add them in one step. Invitations are off by default.

where.path: Awards → (program) → Rounds → (round) → Reviewers → Assign by tag

entries.use_case: When a later round should go to a tagged subset of the panel (say, Senior judges for the final), a program manager can put them all on the round at once instead of editing each reviewer.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: available to program managers on every round.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Awards customer runs multi-round judging with different panels per round.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers who use Reviewer Tags (few today — a good reason to introduce tags).
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Rounds → round → Reviewers → Assign by tag
internal.gotchas: Tags are per program, so only this program's current reviewers match. Logged in the program audit log as Reviewers added by tag.
internal.talk_track: Tag your judges once, then drop a whole tag onto a round — you'll see who's added and who's already there before confirming.

entries.title: Visitors can vote for the posters they rate
entries.summary: Turn on **Attendee voting** on a gallery's **Behavior** tab and every poster carries a vote control, on the card and in the detail view. **Show vote counts** decides whether visitors see the running tally; either way **Most voted posters** ranks them for you on **Analytics**.

enable.path: Publish → Posters → a gallery → Behavior → Attendee voting

where.path: Publish → Posters → a gallery → Behavior

entries.use_case: A poster hall that ran a paper ballot, or no vote at all, can now collect a people's-choice result from the same page visitors are already reading — and see the ranking without counting anything.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on beyond the switch on the gallery's Behavior tab; Poster Gallery itself is still per-event Early Access.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer running a people's-choice or best-poster award, or asking how to measure which posters landed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with a Poster Gallery — scientific and medical meetings with a poster hall above all.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Posters → a gallery → Behavior → Attendee voting
internal.gotchas: A public hall has no sign-in: a vote is tied to the visitor's browser, so clearing site data or a private window lets the same person vote again. On a Gated gallery the vote is tied to the verified email. Do not sell it as a ballot — it is a popularity signal, and a customer awarding a prize on it should say so in their own rules.
internal.talk_track: Visitors can now vote on posters straight from the hall, and you get the ranking in Analytics — it is a popularity read, not a secure ballot.

entries.title: Authors can record a poster narration in the browser
entries.summary: The **Narrate your poster** card on an author's session **Files** tab records a walkthrough of up to five minutes — record, play it back, and **Save narration** or **Discard and record again**. Visitors hear it as **Author narration** next to the poster.

where.path: Speaker portal → My Participation → a poster session → Files → Narrate your poster

entries.use_case: An author who could not get an audio file out of their recording software can now narrate their poster from the portal in two minutes, so a visitor reading it months later still hears them explain it.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on. The card appears on a session that has a live poster when the event has Poster Gallery.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers whose poster halls are read long after the meeting, and anyone who asked for narrated ePosters.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with a Poster Gallery and authors who will not hand over an audio file.
internal.staff_path: View portal as an author → a poster session → Files → Narrate your poster
internal.gotchas: Five minutes and 12 MB. Recording again replaces the previous take — there is no Remove button, though a saved narration can be deleted from the Files list like any other file. The author must allow the microphone; a blocked permission looks like a dead button.
internal.talk_track: Your authors can record a short narration straight from the portal — no software, no file to send you — and visitors hear it beside the poster.

entries.title: Authors can build their poster in the portal
entries.summary: A Poster slot card now offers **Build your poster**: the block editor that organizers use, opened on the author's own session and seeded from the abstract they submitted. **Save draft** keeps the work, **Publish my poster** files it as the session's poster.

where.path: Speaker portal → My Participation → a poster session → Files → Build your poster

entries.use_case: An author with the content but no designed poster can lay one out in the browser from the abstract they already submitted, instead of the organizer building it for them or the session going to the hall empty.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: the link appears on the Poster slot card for events with Poster Gallery.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers chasing authors for poster files, or who have been asking staff to build posters from abstracts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with a Poster Gallery and a long Missing list on Poster coverage.
internal.staff_path: View portal as an author → a poster session → Files → Build your poster
internal.gotchas: A session has one current poster: publishing from the builder replaces an uploaded file as the current one, and an upload afterwards replaces the built one (the earlier file stays in version history). The link only appears in the speaker portal — not on the admin Files list, not in the Public API slot payload.
internal.talk_track: Authors can now build a poster from their abstract in the browser, so a session without a file is not automatically a gap in your hall.

entries.title: Duplicate contacts are suggested from either contact, and any of them can be the primary
entries.summary: Contacts with exactly the same name or email are now always suggested to each other, from either profile. The contact you open is always listed on **Merge Duplicates**, so it can be the primary, and the search box there finds records by email.

where.path: Contact profile → Merge Duplicates

entries.use_case: When the same speaker exists under a work and a personal address, either record now shows the duplicate banner and the admin can keep the one they want as the primary.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on; applies wherever duplicate merging is available (Speaker CRM or Unique Contacts).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that only one of two duplicates shows the banner, or that the record they want to keep is missing from the merge screen.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM and Unique Contacts customers who merge duplicates, especially after imports from several sources.
internal.staff_path: Contact profile → duplicates banner → Merge Duplicates
internal.gotchas: Fuzzy matches (name variants, similar email prefixes) still come from search and can take a few minutes to appear for a new contact; exact name/email matches appear at once.
internal.talk_track: If two records have the same name or email, you'll see the duplicate from either one now, and you can pick whichever record you want to keep.

entries.title: Filter reviewers and email the ones you pick, with your own message
entries.summary: The **Reviewers** list now filters by plan, reviewer tag and status (**Not emailed yet**, **Emailed**, **No assignments**, **Not started**, **In progress**, **Done**), and **Invert** flips the selection across every matching reviewer. **Email** in the selection bar sends just those reviewers their plan invitation again, or a custom subject, message and button with merge tags such as each reviewer's name, assignment count, deadline and portal link. A per-reviewer preview and **Send a test to me** come before the send.

where.path: Program → Review → Reviewers (or a plan's Reviewers tab) → select reviewers → Email

entries.use_case: Mid-review, an admin can filter to the reviewers who have not started, pick them, and send a personal nudge with their own assignment count and a one-click link to their review portal, instead of emailing the whole plan or relying on the generic invitation.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on; it is on every review plan's Reviewers list.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says reviewer emails are too generic, or that the only options are emailing everyone on a plan or resending one invitation at a time.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers running large or multi-plan review committees, especially abstract reviews with hundreds of reviewers.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Reviewers → filters → select → Email
internal.gotchas: A custom email is tied to one plan per send; the plan invitation can go for every open plan a reviewer is on (one email per plan). Custom copy can go to a closed plan, but the reviewer's portal shows nothing until the plan opens. Reviewers selected but not on the chosen plan are skipped and the dialog says so. Up to 5,000 reviewers per send. Test sends carry [Test] in the subject and go only to the admin. A follow-up web-api change limits custom emails to admins who can update review plans.
internal.talk_track: Filter your reviewers to exactly who you need, say everyone who hasn't started, and send them your own message. Each one sees their own name, how many submissions they have, and a button straight into their review portal.

entries.title: Assignments step: select all shown, invert, and remove reviewers from submissions
entries.summary: Under **Individual reviewers** on a review plan's Assignments step, **Select all *N* shown**, **Invert selection** and **Clear** work on the reviewers the search and tag filter show. **Bulk action: Remove reviewers** takes the ticked reviewers off the chosen submissions in the round, with a **Removal preview** first. Only assignments nobody has started are removed; completed reviews, reviews in progress and declines stay.

where.path: Program → Review → plan → Edit → Assignments → Individual reviewers → Bulk action

entries.use_case: When a reviewer group was assigned to the wrong track, or a reviewer drops out, an admin can pull those reviewers off just the affected submissions in one step without touching any review already started or finished.

cs_action.note: On by default for event review plans.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer needs to undo part of an assignment run, or asks how to take a tagged group off a set of submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers who run multi-track or multi-round abstract reviews.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Edit → Assignments → Individual reviewers → Bulk action: Remove reviewers
internal.gotchas: Remove applies to the round selected at the top and the submissions chosen under Which submissions?. It never removes started, completed or declined reviews, and reviewers stay on the plan; to take people off the plan use Remove from plan on the Reviewers tab. Not offered on Speaker CRM interest-form plans.
internal.talk_track: Pick the reviewers, switch the bulk action to Remove, and Sessionboard shows you exactly which open assignments go before anything changes. Started and finished reviews are never touched.

entries.title: Remove reviewers from a plan in bulk, and duplicate a plan without its reviewers
entries.summary: A plan's **Reviewers** tab can filter by tag or **No assignments in this plan** and **Remove from plan** many reviewers at once, after a preview of who stays. **Duplicate plan** now asks whether to **Copy reviewers and their assignments**, and starts unchecked.

where.path: Program → Review → plan → Reviewers tab; Plan Options → Duplicate plan

entries.use_case: A copied plan no longer drags the whole reviewer roster into every reviewer's portal. Admins can duplicate a plan clean, or trim a copied roster down to the people who actually have work in one action.

cs_action.note: On by default.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When reviewers complain about seeing plans they have nothing to do in, usually after an admin duplicated a plan for another track.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers who duplicate review plans per track or per round.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Reviewers tab → filter → select → Remove from plan
internal.gotchas: Reviewers who saved an answer or declined a submission in the plan stay on it; use Remove on their row to take them off anyway. Unstarted assignments go with removed reviewers. Nothing scored is deleted.
internal.talk_track: Duplicate the plan without reviewers, or clean up a copied roster in one go. Anyone who has already reviewed stays.

entries.title: My Reviews lists only the plans where a reviewer has something to do
entries.summary: The review portal's **My Reviews** no longer lists a plan or round where the reviewer has no assignments once that round has been handed out to other reviewers. Rounds nobody has been assigned in yet still show, as **None assigned**.

where.path: Review portal → My Reviews

entries.use_case: Reviewers on a copied or multi-track plan only see the reviews that are theirs, so they stop asking support why a plan shows nothing to do.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When reviewers report plans with 0 of 0 or None assigned on My Reviews.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers who duplicate review plans or run several tracks with one roster.
internal.staff_path: Preview as reviewer in portal → My Reviews
internal.gotchas: A round where nobody has assignments yet stays visible, so reviewers can see work that is coming. Completed and abstained reviews count as work.
internal.talk_track: Your reviewers now only see the plans where they actually have reviews to do.

entries.title: Abstaining for a conflict records a declared conflict, and the conflict audit handles large plans
entries.summary: When a reviewer abstains with a reason that names a conflict relationship, such as **Author**, **Collaborator** or **Institutional affiliation**, Sessionboard records a declared conflict on that one submission, badges it in the conflict audit and keeps later assignment runs from re-assigning the pair. The conflict audit now lists every conflicting assigned pair in the product on large plans instead of asking you to download it.

where.path: Review plan → Reviewers tab → Conflict audit; review portal → Abstain

entries.use_case: Committees that ask reviewers to pick a conflict type when they abstain get those conflicts on record automatically, so the next round doesn't send the same abstract back to its author, and admins can work the audit on screen even with tens of thousands of assignments.

cs_action.note: Automatic for every review plan with abstaining on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer's abstention reasons are conflict types and the declared-conflicts card stays empty, or when the conflict audit said there were too many pairs to show.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific societies running blind or peer abstract review with conflict-of-interest policies.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Reviewers tab → Conflict audit / Declared conflicts
internal.gotchas: The declaration covers that one submission only, never the authors' other submissions or their organization. Reasons like Not qualified to review stay plain abstentions.
internal.talk_track: If a reviewer abstains because they're an author or collaborator, that's now recorded as a conflict on that submission, and you can review every conflict in the audit without downloading anything.

entries.title: Recipient merge tags name the additional contact when you send only to additional contacts
entries.summary: With **Send only to additional contacts of recipients**, `{{{recipient.first_name}}}`, `{{{recipient.last_name}}}` and `{{{recipient.email}}}` now fill in with each additional contact's own details instead of the primary contact's. Other recipient field tags are blank in their email.

where.path: Contacts or Sessions → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts

entries.use_case: An assistant emailed on a speaker's behalf is greeted by their own name, not the speaker's, so emails to coordinators read correctly.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that emails to assistants greeted them with the speaker's name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers' assistants or coordinators through additional contacts.
internal.staff_path: Send Email → Include additional contacts → Send only to additional contacts of recipients → preview
internal.gotchas: Portal login link, sessions summary and module tables still refer to the primary contact, on purpose. Email campaigns' Send individual emails to additional contacts option still renders the primary contact's values.
internal.talk_track: When you email only the assistants, each one now sees their own name in the greeting.

entries.title: Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off, per form
entries.summary: A new form setting, **Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off**, lets submitters paste or type past a Text or Text Area question's **Maximum Length**. The full answer is kept, the counter turns red, a message asks them to shorten it, and **Next** and **Submit** stay blocked until it fits. Off by default, on submission forms, follow-up forms, Awards application forms and interest forms.

enable.path: Submission form → Form Settings → Character limits → Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off

where.path: Submission forms (Form Settings), follow-up forms (Settings step), Awards form builder (Rules tab), interest forms (Details step)

entries.use_case: Submitters who draft abstracts in Word and paste each section no longer lose the end of an answer without noticing. They see exactly how far over they are and trim it themselves, so staff stop emailing people to fix truncated text.

cs_action.note: Off on every form; organizers turn it on per form.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports abstracts or bios arriving cut off, or staff emailing submitters to resend text that was truncated on paste.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific societies with strict abstract limits, and any customer whose submitters paste long answers.
internal.staff_path: Form builder → Form Settings → Character limits (CFP); Settings step (follow-up); Rules tab (Awards); Details step (interest forms)
internal.gotchas: Applies to Text and Text Area questions only; Email, URL and Rich Text keep the hard cap. Event application and intake forms don't have the setting. Duplicating a form copies it. The server refuses an over-limit answer whatever the setting, so nothing over the limit is saved.
internal.talk_track: Turn this on and a submitter who pastes too much sees a red counter and a clear message instead of silently losing the end of their abstract.

entries.title: Upload slots: ask only one kind of submission for a file
entries.summary: An upload slot's new **Applies to** setting limits it to **Top-level submissions only**, **Nested submissions only** (for example the posters inside a poster hall block) or **Abstracts only**, or leaves it on **Every submission**. Submission filters narrow it further, and coverage, reminders and the speaker portal all follow it.

where.path: Program Settings → Files → Upload slots → open a slot → Applies to

entries.use_case: An organizer collecting posters only from the posters nested under a poster session, or slides only from accepted abstracts, can say so on the slot, so other submissions are not asked for the file or reminded about it.

cs_action.note: Existing slots stay on Every submission.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants a file from subsessions or abstracts only and filters can't express it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers with poster halls, nested sessions or abstract programs using upload slots.
internal.staff_path: Program Settings → Files → Upload slots → slot → Applies to
internal.gotchas: A session the slot stops applying to keeps files already uploaded; they show under Submission files in the portal. Insights slot fields do not apply the scope yet.
internal.talk_track: Tell a slot which kind of submission owes the file, and only those speakers are asked and reminded.

entries.title: Review reminder emails show the event name again
entries.summary: The **Review reminder** email to reviewers filled `{{event.name}}` with nothing on some events, so the subject read *Reminder: your reviews for* with no event. The event name now fills in, including in customized templates.

where.path: Review reminder emails sent to reviewers

entries.use_case: Reviewers who serve on several events see which event's reviews are waiting, right in the subject line.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Some customers got blank-subject reminders between Oct 25 and Nov 2; mention the fix if they ask.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer or reviewer reports reminder emails with a blank event name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with review reminders on, especially with a customized reminder template.
internal.staff_path: Settings → System emails → Review reminder
internal.gotchas: The same fix fills {{event.name}} in the weekly portal summary and any other system email that had the gap.
internal.talk_track: Review reminders name the event again, so reviewers know which reviews are waiting.

entries.title: The merge screen shows how many sessions each duplicate holds
entries.summary: On **Merge Duplicates**, the **Select Contacts** table has a new **Sessions** column with each record's live session count, so you can see which record holds the person's work before you choose the primary.

where.path: Contact profile → Merge Duplicates → Select Contacts

entries.use_case: When two records for the same speaker exist, the admin can keep the one their sessions already hang off as the primary, instead of guessing from names and emails.

cs_action.note: Automatic wherever duplicate merging is available (Speaker CRM or Unique Contacts).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks which duplicate to keep as the primary.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM and Unique Contacts customers who merge duplicates.
internal.staff_path: Contact profile → duplicates banner → Merge Duplicates
internal.gotchas: The count is live sessions only. The same release also stops suggesting pairs a super user marked Not a duplicate on the staff-only review page.
internal.talk_track: Before you merge, you can now see how many sessions each record is on, so you keep the right one.

entries.title: Marketing workspace Home is now a persistent AI chat with section tiles, threads and a crew of named robots
entries.summary: The **Home** page of the Marketing workspace is now a full conversational interface powered by **Ask**. Eight section tiles (**Campaigns**, **Pages**, **Recordings**, **Apps**, **Team**, **Follow-up**, **Results**, and **Content**) sit at the top; tapping one opens a thread where the section's robot offers its real actions as chips. Free-text messages route to the matching section automatically. Threads are saved per person per org, pinned to a URL (`?thread=`), and searchable by title — so reloading or sharing a link reopens the conversation exactly where it left off. A **Meet the crew** step lets the org owner name and dress three robots (defaults **Pip**, **Reel** and **Dash**), with hat and outfit choices saved for the whole org; easter eggs unlock a crown at 5 taps and a wizard hat at 12. The setup conversation is pinned as the first thread ("Setting up \<Company\>") and a progress card on Home tracks which sections are done. An optional **Turn on two-step sign-in** card appears in the welcome chat for new trial owners.

where.path: Marketing → Home

entries.use_case: When an organizer sets up a new Marketing workspace, they can chat with Ask on Home to build speaker campaigns, draft an event page, connect apps and review results — all from one place, without navigating between separate setup screens. The thread history means they can pause, come back, and pick up exactly where they left off.

cs_action.note: This is a large new surface for the Marketing workspace (limited_release). Confirm the customer's workspace is provisioned before walking them through it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a customer onto the Marketing workspace or when they ask how to get started with speaker promotion, event pages or app connections.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with access to the Marketing workspace (limited_release), especially new trial owners going through initial setup.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Home (org-level, /marketing/:orgId)
internal.gotchas: The AI routing is deterministic for now — there is no live model call. Actions without a runner yet (collect videos, post pack, library) surface a message and open the section page instead. The setup conversation thread is pinned and cannot be deleted. Two-step sign-in offer only appears for trial owners with the marketing_trial exemption reason. Copy is English only; no locale keys yet.
internal.talk_track: Home in your Marketing workspace is now a chat — tap a tile for Campaigns, Pages or any other section and Ask walks you through the real setup steps. Your threads are saved, so you can pause and come back, and the crew of robots your team names shows up on every section card.

draft.docs_gap: The what-is-sessionboard-marketing guide should add a section describing the Ask-powered Home, the section tiles, thread persistence via ?thread=, the Meet the crew robot customisation step, and the setup progress card.
draft.why_use_it: The Marketing workspace brings speaker promotion, event pages, recordings, apps and results into one place for event organizers. Ask on Home lets you start any of those workflows by typing what you want to happen or tapping a section tile — no hunting through menus. Threads keep a record of every action taken so you can return to a conversation, share a link with a colleague, or review what was set up. The crew of named robots gives your workspace a consistent identity across every section card.

entries.title: Sign in to Sessionboard Marketing with an email code, and invite teammates
entries.summary: A new **Sign in** page (`/signin`) lets Marketing workspace owners and teammates enter their work email and receive a 6-digit one-time code to access their workspace — no password required. A new **Team** card on the workspace home and at the end of sign-up lets owners invite colleagues by email, view pending invites, and cancel them; adding the first teammate automatically enables two-step sign-in for the whole workspace. The `/login` page now links "Using Sessionboard Marketing? Get a sign-in code" for users who land there by mistake.

where.path: sessionboard.com/signin · Marketing workspace home → Team

entries.use_case: Marketing workspace accounts are created without a password, so this gives owners and their teammates a secure, frictionless way back in — and a built-in flow to grow the team — without needing IT to set up SSO or manage credentials.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all Marketing (beta) customers. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing customer asks how to get back into their workspace or how to add a colleague to their account.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with access to the Sessionboard Marketing beta workspace.
internal.staff_path: sessionboard.com/signin
internal.gotchas: Adding the first teammate automatically enables two-step sign-in for the entire workspace — flag this to customers who may not expect the behaviour change. If a user has a password or SSO, the sign-in page routes them to /login or /sso respectively. 2FA challenges are handed off to /login and are consumed on load so a page reload cannot replay them.
internal.talk_track: Marketing workspace users now have a dedicated sign-in page — just enter your work email, get a 6-digit code, and you're in. You can also invite your whole team directly from the workspace home, and the first invite you send automatically turns on two-step sign-in for everyone.

draft.docs_gap: The Marketing guide should add a section covering the /signin email-code flow, the Team card (inviting, viewing, and cancelling invites), and the automatic two-step sign-in behaviour triggered by the first teammate invite.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing gives event teams a dedicated workspace to plan, produce and distribute content across the full event lifecycle. Because Marketing accounts are separate from the main Sessionboard login, the email-code sign-in flow keeps access simple and secure for everyone on the team. Use the Team card to bring colleagues in so they can collaborate on content, campaigns and brand assets from day one.

entries.title: Sign up for Sessionboard Marketing without contacting sales
entries.summary: A new chat-style sign-up flow at **/signup** lets anyone start a Sessionboard Marketing trial without contacting sales. Enter a work email, verify with a 6-digit code, answer a few setup questions about your role, website and event, and a ready-to-use Marketing workspace is created automatically — including a first event with the correct contacts record types. A 14-day trial begins immediately; two-factor authentication is not required during the trial for the sole workspace owner.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Marketing self-serve sign-up; then visit /signup

where.path: /signup (public sign-up page)

entries.use_case: When a marketing team wants to evaluate Sessionboard Marketing, they can sign up and get a working workspace in minutes using only a work email — no sales call or manual provisioning required. The trial includes a pre-configured event so they can explore speaker and session management immediately.

cs_action.note: The flow is gated behind the MARKETING_SIGNUP_ENABLED flag; it is off in all environments until explicitly turned on. Coordinate with engineering before directing any customer to /signup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or existing customer asks how to try Sessionboard Marketing without going through a full sales cycle.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing teams and event organizers evaluating Sessionboard Marketing for the first time.
internal.staff_path: /signup (only accessible once the feature flag is enabled in that environment)
internal.gotchas: Personal and throwaway email domains are blocked at sign-up — only work emails are accepted. The 2FA grace period applies only to the sole owner of the trial workspace; adding a teammate immediately restores normal 2FA enforcement. The first event is created via createLightEvent; events created before this change (via the old createOrgEvent path) may still throw 'No record type was found' when adding a speaker.
internal.talk_track: You can now start a Sessionboard Marketing trial directly from the sign-up page using your work email — no sales call needed. You'll get a 14-day trial with a pre-built event so you can start exploring right away.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started overview should add a section describing the self-serve Marketing sign-up flow, including the work-email requirement, the 6-digit verification step, the onboarding questions, the 14-day trial terms, and the 2FA grace-period behaviour for trial owners.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing brings speaker content, session recordings, slides, clips and social distribution into one place so event teams produce and share content without juggling separate tools. A self-serve trial lets you explore the full workflow — from collecting speaker submissions to publishing clips and running Advocacy campaigns — at your own pace. Use it when you want to see how Marketing fits your event before committing to a plan.

entries.title: Poster Gallery hall now inherits branding from the Brand kit
entries.summary: The **Appearance** tab in the Poster Gallery builder gains a **Brand** card that shows which Brand kit the hall is using and how it was chosen. Every branded control — accent colour, logo, banner — displays an **InheritedMark** showing the kit source (e.g. *From Northwind Health*) while it follows the kit, and lets organizers override individual values or revert to inherited. New controls include a **Heading font** field and a **Page background** selector (**Inherit / Plain / Accent wash / Image**). The public hall paints the resolved canvas — image backgrounds carry an automatic scrim for contrast, and a wash renders as a soft accent gradient — and loads the kit's heading font from Google Fonts for headings only.

where.path: Marketing → Poster Gallery → [gallery] → Appearance

entries.use_case: Organizers who maintain a Brand kit no longer need to manually copy colours, logos and fonts into each poster hall — the hall picks them up automatically, so every gallery stays on-brand without extra effort. Individual overrides are still available when a specific hall needs a different look.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for customers with Poster Gallery (beta) and Brand kit (limited_release) access. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their poster hall looks different from the rest of their event branding, or when they are setting up Brand kits and want to know which surfaces benefit.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Poster Gallery who also have Brand kits configured.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Poster Gallery → any gallery → Appearance tab → Brand card
internal.gotchas: The new background, font and brand_kit_id fields are only sent to the API once the API ships the matching release (web-api#5161). Until then, the Appearance tab renders as before — the Brand card and InheritedMarks appear but saves omit the new fields, so no existing gallery data is affected.
internal.talk_track: Your poster halls now read from your Brand kit automatically — same logo, colours and heading font as the rest of your event. You can still override any value per gallery, and reverting always goes back to the live kit rather than a frozen copy.

draft.docs_gap: The poster-gallery guide should add a section explaining Brand kit inheritance in the Appearance tab: the Brand card, InheritedMark behaviour, the new Heading font and Page background controls, and how the public hall renders image/wash/plain backgrounds.
draft.why_use_it: Poster galleries give attendees and the public a browsable, visual index of your event's research and session content. Connecting them to your Brand kit means the hall's colours, logo, heading font and background stay consistent with the rest of your event marketing without any manual copying. Override individual values when a specific gallery needs a distinct look, and revert to inherited at any time to follow the kit again.

entries.title: Sign in to a Marketing workspace with a code, and invite teammates
entries.summary: Marketing workspace accounts created through the sign-up flow can now sign back in using a 6-digit email code — no password required. Workspace owners can also invite up to 20 teammates at once; each invitee receives a Marketing email with a **Sign in** link and joins using the same code-based flow.

where.path: Marketing workspace → Sign in / Team

entries.use_case: Marketing workspace owners whose accounts were created without a password can now return to their workspace at any time using a one-time email code. They can also bring colleagues in by entering their email addresses, so the whole team works from the same workspace without needing to set up passwords.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for Marketing workspace customers. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing workspace customer says they cannot get back in after their session expired, or when they ask how to add colleagues to their workspace.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using or trialling the Marketing workspace who need persistent access or want to collaborate with teammates.
internal.staff_path: Marketing workspace → Sign in page (code flow) / Team card (invite)
internal.gotchas: Code sign-in is only available to Marketing workspace members on a non-SSO domain. SSO and password accounts follow their existing flows. The first teammate invited ends the 2FA trial grace period for the whole workspace, consistent with password sign-in behaviour. Seat limits are not enforced yet — billing limits land in a follow-up branch.
internal.talk_track: If you signed up for a Marketing workspace and couldn't get back in, you can now sign in with a 6-digit code sent to your email. And if you want your team working alongside you, just enter their email addresses from the team card — they'll get a link and sign in the same way.

draft.docs_gap: The Marketing overview guide should add a section explaining code-based sign-in for passwordless accounts and how workspace owners invite teammates, including the invite limit, the email teammates receive, and how 2FA interacts with the trial grace period.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing gives event teams a shared workspace to produce, organise and distribute content across slides, clips, carousels and social channels. Code-based sign-in means anyone on the team gets back in with just their email address — no password to set or reset. Inviting teammates lets multiple people contribute to the same workspace so content production and distribution are a team effort rather than a solo task.

entries.title: Poster galleries inherit branding from the Brand kit
entries.summary: A poster gallery's **Appearance** tab now resolves its accent colour, logo, heading font, and canvas background from the event's **Brand kit** instead of requiring every value to be set by hand. Values set directly on the gallery override the kit; clearing an override hands that value back to the kit. Galleries that already have a logo stored show it as an override — clicking **Use the brand kit** restores inheritance.

where.path: Program → Poster Gallery → [gallery] → Appearance

entries.use_case: When an organizer updates their event's Brand kit — changing the accent colour or swapping the logo — every poster gallery that has not set its own override reflects the change automatically, keeping the hall on-brand without touching each gallery individually.

cs_action.note: Existing galleries that had a logo copied at creation time will appear as 'overridden'. Customers may need to click 'Use the brand kit' on each gallery to restore inheritance. Worth flagging proactively for accounts with many galleries.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their poster hall looks different from their other branded surfaces, or when they are setting up Brand kits and want consistent branding everywhere.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Poster Gallery (beta) who also have a Brand kit configured.
internal.staff_path: Program → Poster Gallery → [any gallery] → Appearance
internal.gotchas: Galleries created before this change may carry a frozen logo from the event's logo at creation time — they will show as 'overridden' and need a one-click reset. The banner image has no kit equivalent and still defaults to the event's background image. The public hall page never exposes the kit ID or kit name to visitors.
internal.talk_track: Your poster halls now pull their accent colour, logo, heading font, and background from your Brand kit automatically. If a hall has its own look, you can still override any value individually — and clearing it hands it straight back to the kit.

draft.docs_gap: The poster-gallery guide should add a section explaining Brand kit inheritance on the Appearance tab: which values come from the kit (accent colour, logo, heading font, canvas background), how per-gallery overrides work, and how to restore inheritance with "Use the brand kit".
draft.why_use_it: Poster galleries display research posters and abstracts in a branded, public-facing hall. Connecting the hall to the Brand kit means the accent colour, logo, heading font, and canvas background stay consistent with the rest of the event's marketing surfaces without manual upkeep. Individual galleries can still override any value when a specific hall needs its own look, and clearing that override hands the value straight back to the kit.

entries.title: History now labels title-slide generation as "Generation requested"
entries.summary: When an organizer triggers a title-slide generation run, the **History** audit log and the **Action** filter now show the entry as **Generation requested** (in English, German, Spanish and French), accurately reflecting that the job is queued rather than instantly complete.

where.path: Communications → History → Audit (Action filter)

entries.use_case: Organizers auditing slide generation activity can now correctly identify title-slide generation jobs in the History log — the action label matches what actually happened (a queued request) rather than implying the deck was already finished.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports confusion about what the title-slide History entry means, or asks why the action filter label did not match the generate action.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Slides with title-slide generation.
internal.staff_path: Communications → History → Audit; filter by Action = Generation requested
internal.gotchas: The label change applies to new History rows only; existing rows created before this fix retain their old label.
internal.talk_track: The History audit log now correctly labels title-slide generation jobs as 'Generation requested', so the Action filter matches what you see in the log.

draft.docs_gap: The History guide's Audit section should note that title-slide generation appears as "Generation requested" because the job is queued asynchronously, and list it alongside other auditable Marketing actions.

entries.title: Set an opens and closes window for a poster gallery
entries.summary: Poster galleries now have an **Opens at** and **Closes at** date-time pair, replacing the single embargo date. Either bound is optional and independently clearable, so a gallery can open at a fixed time, close at a fixed time, or both. When a narration recording is held because the gallery is not yet open, the author's portal player shows a message explaining why — instead of an empty player — so authors know their recording is safe.

where.path: Program → Poster Gallery → Gallery settings → Opens at / Closes at

entries.use_case: Conference organizers who run a poster hall with a strict embargo can now set both an opening and a closing time on the gallery, so posters are automatically hidden before the conference opens and after it ends — no manual toggling required. Poster authors who have recorded a narration will see a clear hold message in their portal instead of a blank player, so they know their recording is intact.

cs_action.note: The new Opens at / Closes at fields replace the old single embargo date. Existing embargo dates are migrated to opens_at automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to hide posters until the conference opens, or wants the hall to close automatically after the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any Poster Gallery beta customer running a timed poster hall or abstract embargo.
internal.staff_path: Program → Poster Gallery → Gallery settings
internal.gotchas: The S3 object tag is still named 'embargo' internally — this is intentional and does not affect the product UI. The Approval_Policies embargo_mode and Content_Galleries embargo_config are separate features and are not changed.
internal.talk_track: You can now set both an opening and a closing time on your poster gallery — the hall opens and closes automatically, and authors see a clear message in their portal if their narration is on hold rather than an empty player.

draft.docs_gap: The guide's "Embargo and author consent" section should be updated to describe the new Opens at / Closes at pair, explain that either bound is optional, and note what poster authors see in their portal when a narration is held during a closed window.
draft.why_use_it: The poster gallery open/close window gives you precise control over when your poster hall is visible to attendees. Set an opening time to enforce a pre-conference embargo, a closing time to retire the hall after the event, or both — each bound is independent and optional. Authors always see the status of their narration recording in their portal, so they can trust their work is saved even when the hall is closed.

entries.title: Poster Studio replaces the poster builder, with an opens/closes window and held-narration states
entries.summary: The route previously used for the poster builder is now the **Poster Studio** — a three-panel view where authors see their poster exactly as visitors do (**centre**), manage versions, upload a new version, download, access the organiser's template and record narration (**left**), and read the organiser thread (**right**). Organizers can now set an **Opens** / **Closes** window on a poster gallery (replacing the old "embargo" controls). When a narration is held, the **Narration** card tells the author which hold applies — embargoed with a release date, awaiting approval, or denied — so they know whether to record again.

where.path: Speaker portal → poster task → Open poster (Poster Studio); Poster Gallery → builder → Access tab (opens/closes window)

entries.use_case: Authors arrive at the Poster Studio with a finished file and can upload a new version, preview exactly what visitors see, and understand why their narration is on hold — all without leaving the portal. Organizers can gate gallery visibility with an opens/closes window instead of a manual embargo toggle.

cs_action.note: This UI half requires the matching API release (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5170) to ship together. Merging the UI first puts a page in prod that reads fields the live API does not yet send — confirm the API release has cut before pointing customers at the Poster Studio.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Poster Gallery asks how authors manage their poster files, or when they want to control gallery visibility by date.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events already on the Poster Gallery beta that have authors uploading PDFs, decks or videos and recording narration.
internal.staff_path: Speaker portal → poster task → Open poster; Poster Gallery → Access tab
internal.gotchas: The UI reads opens_at / closes_at / closed_mode / window_state and held; the old embargo_until / embargo_mode / embargo_active keys are gone from the API in #5170. Both PRs must be live simultaneously. Video posters do not get a narration option (video carries its own audio). Upload goes straight to the lineage root — no staging step.
internal.talk_track: Authors now land in a Poster Studio that shows their poster exactly as visitors see it, lets them upload a new version in one step, and tells them clearly if their narration is held and why. You can also set an opens and closes date on the gallery so it's only visible during your conference window.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Poster Studio layout (left/centre/right panels), the opens/closes window settings on the Access tab, and the held-narration states (embargoed, awaiting approval, denied) that authors see in the Narration card.
draft.why_use_it: The Poster Gallery lets authors share research posters, slide decks, images and videos with event attendees through a dedicated gallery. Authors upload and version their files, record narration, and track organiser feedback from a single studio view. Organizers control who can see the gallery and when, and can hold narrations for review before they go live.

entries.title: Filter a poster gallery by session fields, scope and subsession grouping
entries.summary: Three new controls are available when building a **Poster Gallery**: **Session filters** lets you apply the same filter rows used elsewhere in the program (field, operator, value) to narrow which posters appear in the hall; **Session scope** lets you restrict the gallery to abstracts, scheduled sessions, subsessions, or all of the above; and **Group subsessions by parent** controls whether subsessions are displayed under their parent session in the hall. A new **Preview** action shows the resulting hall before you save.

where.path: Program → Poster Gallery → Gallery → Edit → Content filters

entries.use_case: An organizer running a research track can build a gallery that shows only accepted abstracts tagged to that track — using the same filter logic they already use in the sessions grid — without manually curating a list of session IDs. The live preview lets them confirm the right posters appear before publishing.

cs_action.note: The new filter controls appear automatically inside the gallery builder for any event with Poster Gallery enabled. No migration of existing galleries is needed — legacy facets (track_ids, format_ids, statuses, etc.) continue to work exactly as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to show only a subset of posters (e.g., one track, only accepted abstracts, or subsessions grouped under their parent) without hand-picking session IDs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any Poster Gallery beta customer, especially those running multi-track or abstract-heavy programs.
internal.staff_path: Program → Poster Gallery → Gallery → Edit → Content filters
internal.gotchas: Session filters are evaluated in the application layer (not SQL), so very large session sets may be slower to resolve. Existing galleries are unaffected — their legacy facets still apply and compose with the new filters via AND.
internal.talk_track: You can now filter your poster hall the same way you filter sessions — by track, status, custom field, tag, or any combination — and preview the result before you publish.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Session filters, Session scope and Group subsessions by parent controls in the gallery builder, and explain how they compose with existing facets (track_ids, format_ids, etc.) and how to use the Preview action.
draft.why_use_it: Poster galleries let you publish an interactive hall where attendees browse, vote on, and bookmark posters or abstracts directly from the event app or a public link. Session filters, scope and subsession grouping give you precise control over which content appears, so a single gallery can serve a specific track, award category, or presentation type without manual curation. The preview mode lets you see the exact hall visitors will experience before you commit any changes.

entries.title: Filter posters in a gallery by any session field, scope, and parent grouping
entries.summary: The **Content** tab in the Poster Gallery builder now includes a full **Filters** row builder — the same component used in the sessions list and evaluation-plan wizard — so you can narrow a gallery by any session field (track, format, room, status, custom fields, and more) with multi-select operators. Two new controls sit alongside it: **Include** lets you choose abstracts, sessions, subsessions, or all; and **Group by parent session** collapses subsessions under their parent for display. Legacy format and track checkboxes remain visible only on galleries that already have them set.

where.path: Program → Poster Gallery → [gallery] → Edit → Content

entries.use_case: An organizer running a clinical conference can show only accepted abstracts in the Clinical track whose Room field is filled — without touching the legacy checkboxes — so the hall opens with exactly the right posters on day one. Subsession-heavy programs can also group child sessions under their parent for a cleaner browsing experience.

cs_action.note: The new filter builder is available to all Poster Gallery beta customers automatically; no flag to flip.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to show only a subset of posters (e.g. one track, one format, or only accepted abstracts) or is confused about why unrelated sessions appear in their gallery.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any Poster Gallery beta customer with multiple tracks, formats, or session types who needs to curate what the hall shows.
internal.staff_path: Program → Poster Gallery → [gallery] → Edit → Content
internal.gotchas: Requires API build #5162 to be deployed; without it the API rejects the new session_filters payload. Legacy format/track checkboxes are hidden on new galleries but still AND with filters on existing ones — warn customers not to expect them on a freshly created gallery.
internal.talk_track: You can now filter your poster hall by any session field — track, room, status, custom fields — the same way you filter the sessions list. You can also choose whether to show abstracts, sessions, subsessions, or all, and group subsessions under their parent.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Filters row builder, the Include (scope) selector, and the Group by parent session toggle in the Content tab, including how incomplete filter rows are ignored and how legacy checkboxes behave on existing galleries.
draft.why_use_it: Poster galleries let you publish a curated, browsable hall of posters and abstracts directly from your program data — no manual uploads or separate tools. Filters, scope controls, and grouping options give you precise control over which sessions appear, so the gallery always reflects the right slice of your program for your audience.

entries.title: Review, flag and dismiss duplicate contact suggestions across your organisation
entries.summary: A new duplicate-review workflow lets admins see an org-wide list of potential duplicate contacts, grouped by person. Pairs are detected automatically by a nightly scan (name matching) and can also be **flagged** by hand. Each pair can be **dismissed** (marked "not a duplicate") or restored, and dismissals survive future scans. A **Re-scan** button triggers an on-demand refresh. Badge counts surface how many open pairs need attention.

where.path: Contacts → Duplicate Suggestions

entries.use_case: Organisations with large contact databases can now find and triage duplicate contacts in one place instead of spotting them one profile at a time. Admins can dismiss false positives so they never resurface, and flag pairs the automatic scan missed, keeping the contact list clean before merging.

cs_action.note: The UI is gated behind useSuperUser() in the companion web-ui-v2 PR (not yet merged). The API endpoints and nightly scan job are live, but the review page is not visible to customers until the front-end ships. No action needed until the UI PR merges.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains about duplicate contacts, manual merging overhead, or data quality in their org directory — especially large orgs (1,000+ contacts).
internal.who_should_get_it: All orgs with the Contacts module; most valuable for large orgs like AUA (26k contacts) that currently merge duplicates by hand.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → Duplicate Suggestions
internal.gotchas: Slice A only: the default rule matches on first + last name (exact or trigram-similar ≥ 0.7). Custom rules are Slice B. The per-contact ES duplicate banner does not yet hide dismissed pairs — that follows in SB-11006. Nothing runs for an org until someone opens the review page or clicks Re-scan for the first time.
internal.talk_track: Instead of hunting for duplicates one profile at a time, you now get an org-wide list of likely duplicates grouped by person. You can dismiss false positives so they never come back, flag pairs the system missed, and then merge from the same place.

draft.docs_gap: The /contacts/merge-duplicates guide should add a section explaining the new org-wide Duplicate Suggestions list, how the nightly scan works, and how to flag, dismiss and restore pairs before merging.
draft.why_use_it: Duplicate contacts cause confusion when the same person appears twice in your directory, receives duplicate emails, or has their history split across records. The duplicate-review workflow surfaces likely duplicates across your entire organisation automatically, groups them by person, and lets you decide what to do with each pair — merge, dismiss or flag — so your contact list stays accurate over time.

entries.title: Define custom duplicate-detection rules for contacts (Enterprise)
entries.summary: Enterprise orgs can now create their own contact duplicate rules instead of relying solely on the default name-matching rule. Each rule ANDs up to 5 conditions — choosing from standard fields (**First + last name**, **First name**, **Last name**, **Email**, **Organization**, **Mobile phone**) or any text, email, phone, number, or URL contact field — with **Exact** or **Similar** matching per condition. Enabled rules replace the default rule and drive the duplicate suggestions queue; the **Duplicate Suggestions** review page shows which rule and fields flagged each pair.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Custom Duplicate Rules; then Organization → Contacts → Duplicate Suggestions → Rules

where.path: Organization → Contacts → Duplicate Suggestions → Rules

entries.use_case: Associations or medical societies that track members by a custom ID field (e.g. "AUA ID") can create a rule that flags contacts sharing the same member ID as duplicates — catching records that a name-only rule would miss. Orgs with contacts who use multiple name variations can combine last name + organization matching to surface likely duplicates without generating false positives.

cs_action.note: The org feature flag 'custom_duplicate_rules' must be toggled on in Org Admin Settings before the Rules UI appears. It is part of the Enterprise CRM package.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Enterprise CRM customer complains that duplicate suggestions miss records with different name spellings, or when they track contacts by a member ID or external CRM key.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise orgs with large contact databases, membership associations, or medical/professional societies that assign unique member IDs.
internal.staff_path: Org Admin Settings → Features & Enhancements → Custom Duplicate Rules
internal.gotchas: Up to 10 rules per org; each rule supports up to 5 conditions with no repeated fields. 'First + last name' cannot be combined with standalone First name or Last name in the same rule. Dismissed pairs stay dismissed even if a rule change would re-match them — the scan never resets dismissal status. With all custom rules disabled, the org falls back to the default name rule.
internal.talk_track: If your team tracks speakers or members by a custom ID, you can now tell Sessionboard to flag contacts that share the same ID as duplicates — so you catch records that look different on the surface but are actually the same person.

draft.docs_gap: The merge-duplicates guide should add a section explaining how Enterprise admins create, edit, enable and delete custom duplicate rules, including the field and mode options and the 10-rule / 5-condition limits.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard automatically scans your contacts for duplicates and surfaces pairs for review, so your CRM stays clean without manual searching. Custom duplicate rules let you define exactly which fields — including your own custom contact fields — determine whether two records are the same person, using either exact or fuzzy matching. This is especially useful when your contacts are identified by a member ID, a secondary email, or an external CRM key that the default name rule cannot see.

entries.title: Find, review and resolve possible duplicate contacts from a dedicated duplicates page
entries.summary: A new **Possible duplicates** page at **Contacts → Possible duplicates** lists contacts the system has flagged as likely duplicates, grouped into side-by-side cards that highlight differing fields (email, organization, title, phone, portal login, events, linked sessions) and show "Why suggested" chips explaining the match rule. From the page, organizers can **Merge** a group, dismiss the whole group with **Not a duplicate** (with an **Undo** toast), or dismiss a single pair within a larger group. The **Dismissed** tab shows every dismissed pair with who dismissed it and when, and lets organizers undo. The org contacts directory gains a **Possible duplicates (N)** filter chip, a **Review duplicates (N)** button, a *Possible duplicate* badge on flagged rows, and a **Mark as possible duplicates** bulk action (2–20 contacts). Each contact profile also shows a *Possible duplicates* card and a **Mark as possible duplicate** action with contact search.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable this feature; then Contacts → Possible duplicates

where.path: Contacts → Possible duplicates (dedicated page); Contacts directory (filter chip, badge, bulk action); Contact profile (Possible duplicates card)

entries.use_case: When a contact database has grown across many events, organizers can use the Possible duplicates page to systematically find and merge duplicate records — or dismiss false positives — without manually hunting through the directory. The directory filter and contact-profile card let organizers act on duplicates in context, wherever they spot them.

cs_action.note: Visible to super users only in this slice. CS must enable for a customer org before any organizer can see the page, directory additions, or profile card.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains about duplicate contacts across events, or asks how to clean up their CRM before a new event cycle.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs with large multi-event contact databases where duplicates accumulate over time; CRM add-on customers.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → Possible duplicates
internal.gotchas: This is Slice A — super-user-gated. The Merge button passes ?with=<ids> but the merge page does not yet preselect contacts (that lands in a follow-up PR, SB-11006 / #1491). Bulk 'Mark as possible duplicates' requires selecting 2–20 contacts. API calls fail silently (404 hides the badge, filter and card) so a stale link on an older API version will not error.
internal.talk_track: We now automatically surface contacts that look like duplicates — you can review them side by side, see exactly why they were flagged, and merge or dismiss them in one place. You can also manually flag two contacts as duplicates from the directory or a contact profile.

draft.docs_gap: The merge-duplicates guide should add a section covering the new Possible duplicates page, the directory filter chip and badge, the contact-profile card, the manual Mark as possible duplicate action, and the dismiss/undo workflow.
draft.why_use_it: Duplicate contacts fragment speaker history, skew reporting and cause confusion when the same person receives multiple portal invitations. The Possible duplicates tools surface likely matches automatically — based on name similarity, email, and other signals — and let organizers review them side by side, merge the ones that are real duplicates, and dismiss the ones that are not, keeping the contact database clean over time.

entries.title: Define custom rules for which contacts are flagged as possible duplicates
entries.summary: A new **Rules** tab on the **Possible Duplicates** page lets organizers create, enable, and manage up to 10 custom duplicate-detection rules. Each rule has a name and 1–5 field conditions (built-in or custom text fields, each set to **Exact** or **Similar** matching); the page shows the active rule summary ("Using your N enabled rules") and triggers a background re-scan after any change. Without the Enterprise feature, the tab shows the default rule read-only with no editing controls.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Possible Duplicates Enterprise feature; then Contacts → Possible Duplicates → Rules

where.path: Contacts → Possible Duplicates → Rules

entries.use_case: An org that tracks members by a proprietary ID can create a rule matching on that exact ID field, so the duplicate list surfaces real duplicates instead of contacts who happen to share a common name. Teams with complex data can layer up to 10 rules — any enabled rule that matches will surface a suggestion.

cs_action.note: The Rules tab and editing controls require the Enterprise Possible Duplicates feature flag. Without it the tab shows a read-only explanation. Coordinate with engineering or use the staff console to enable the `available: true` flag for the org.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains that the default name-similarity rule produces too many false positives, or when they have a unique identifier field (member ID, AUA ID, etc.) they want to use for deduplication.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise orgs with large contact databases or proprietary member/attendee ID fields who need precise duplicate detection.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → Possible Duplicates → Rules
internal.gotchas: Feature is super-user / Enterprise only in this slice. If the GET /rules API route is absent (older API), the Rules tab is hidden entirely and ?tab=rules falls back to Open. Limit is 10 rules per org; Add rule is disabled at the limit. Saving a rule triggers a background re-scan; the page shows 'Scanning…' during that time.
internal.talk_track: If the default name-matching rule is surfacing too many false positives, or you have a unique ID field you'd rather match on, you can now define your own duplicate rules — up to 10 — each with the exact fields and match strictness that make sense for your data.

draft.docs_gap: The merge-duplicates guide should add a section explaining the Rules tab: how to create, enable and delete custom rules, the Exact vs Similar distinction, the 10-rule limit, and how enabled rules replace the default name rule.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's duplicate detection compares contacts across your organization and surfaces pairs that look like the same person so you can merge them and keep your CRM clean. Custom rules let you decide which fields — and how strictly — determine a match, so the suggestions reflect your data model rather than a one-size-fits-all name comparison. Rules are ANDed within a rule and ORed across rules, dismissed suggestions stay dismissed, and merges are always a deliberate action — the rules only influence what is suggested.

entries.title: Skip reviewers with no assignments when emailing from a review plan
entries.summary: When emailing selected reviewers from a review plan, the **Email selected** dialog now detects how many of the selected reviewers have no assignments in the chosen plan and shows a message such as "X of the selected have no assignments in this plan." A default-on **Skip them** checkbox excludes those reviewers from the send, the dry-run count, and the preview stepping. The **Email** bulk action on the Reviewers directory is also now shown only to users who have permission to update evaluation plans.

where.path: Program → Review → [Plan] → Reviewers → select reviewers → Email selected

entries.use_case: Events with large reviewer rosters — where many people are on the plan but only a subset have actual assignments — can now email only the reviewers who have work to do, avoiding noise for everyone else. The **Skip them** checkbox is on by default so the safer behaviour requires no extra steps.

cs_action.note: Default-on behaviour; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that reviewers with no assignments are receiving emails, or when a customer with a large roster (e.g. 1,000+ reviewers, only ~200 assigned) asks how to target only active reviewers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Sessions 2.0 customers who use bulk email from review plans and have reviewers on the roster who are not yet assigned.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → [Plan] → Reviewers → select reviewers → Email selected
internal.gotchas: The skip logic requires one plan to be selected in the dialog; with multiple plans chosen the unassigned check does not run. If the API endpoint is older and returns an error, the dialog falls back silently and sends to all selected reviewers with no warning.
internal.talk_track: If you have a big reviewer roster but only some people have assignments yet, the email dialog now tells you how many have nothing to review and skips them by default — so you're not spamming people who aren't ready to start.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Skip them checkbox, the unassigned-reviewer count message, and the permission requirement for the Email bulk action on the Reviewers directory.
draft.why_use_it: Emailing reviewers directly from a review plan lets you reach the right people without leaving the evaluation workflow. The dialog shows a live preview of each message, a dry-run count, and now surfaces reviewers who have nothing assigned so you can exclude them in one click. Use it whenever you need to nudge, remind, or brief your review committee mid-cycle.
